findings.title: Uncapped liability for BAA and privacy violations
findings.deviation: The contract explicitly carves out BAA breaches and privacy events from any liability caps in the Master Services Agreement, making AtliQ's liability unlimited.
findings.impact: AtliQ faces unlimited financial exposure for data incidents, which violates the core risk management principle of capping liability at 1x fees.
findings.quote: The obligations of Business Associate under this Article 8 are not subject to any limitation or exclusion of liability, and shall apply notwithstanding any limitation of liability in the Master Services Agreement.
findings.counterPosition: Liability for data-protection and privacy incidents should be subject to a separate super-cap, such as 2x fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim.

findings.title: Cyber insurance requirement exceeds current coverage
findings.deviation: The BAA requires AtliQ to maintain $5,000,000 in cyber liability insurance, but AtliQ currently only holds $1,000,000.
findings.impact: AtliQ would be in immediate violation of the contract upon signing unless it significantly increases its insurance premiums at its own cost.
findings.quote: Business Associate shall maintain, throughout the term of this BAA and for three (3) years thereafter, cyber liability and network security and privacy insurance with limits of not less than Five Million U.S. Dollars ($5,000,000) per claim and in the aggregate
findings.counterPosition: Align the required insurance limits with AtliQ's current coverage of $1,000,000 per claim and in the aggregate.

findings.title: One-way uncapped indemnity for privacy events
findings.deviation: AtliQ is required to indemnify the client for any losses related to privacy events or HIPAA violations on a one-way basis and without a financial cap.
findings.impact: AtliQ may be forced to pay for all client losses, including regulatory fines and legal fees, even if the client's own systems contributed to the incident.
findings.quote: Business Associate shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Covered Entity, its Affiliates and their respective trustees, officers, employees and agents from and against any and all Losses arising out of or relating to (a) any Privacy Event involving Business Associate or any Subcontractor; (b) any breach of this BAA... (c) any violation of HIPAA or Texas Privacy Law
findings.counterPosition: The indemnity should be mutual, covering each party's own breach or negligence, and must be subject to the agreed liability cap.

findings.title: Prohibition on offshore data access and processing
findings.deviation: The BAA prohibits any access, viewing, or processing of PHI from locations outside the United States, effectively barring AtliQ's Indian delivery teams.
findings.impact: AtliQ cannot utilize its standard global delivery model or its Pune-based entity for this engagement, which may significantly increase costs or prevent project delivery.
findings.quote: Business Associate shall not, and shall ensure that no Subcontractor shall, access, view, create, receive, maintain, transmit, store or process PHI from or at any location outside the United States, whether directly or by remote access.
findings.counterPosition: Allow for offshore access by AtliQ's Indian affiliate (AtliQ Technologies Pvt Ltd) provided that appropriate security controls or de-identification methods are used.

findings.title: One-sided immediate termination of the MSA
findings.deviation: The client has the right to immediately terminate the entire Master Services Agreement based on its own determination of a material BAA violation.
findings.impact: AtliQ's primary contract could be cancelled without notice or a mandatory cure period if the client perceives a data issue.
findings.quote: If Covered Entity determines that Business Associate has violated a material term of this BAA, Covered Entity may, at its option... (b) immediately terminate this BAA and the Master Services Agreement if cure is not possible.
findings.counterPosition: Ensure that termination for cause is mutual and that AtliQ has a 30-day period to cure any remediable violation before termination takes effect.

fine.note: Ownership of PHI and derived data remains with the client, which is standard for health data processing.
Texas law is used for AtliQ Inc, which is an acceptable US state law per the playbook.
Confidentiality obligations for health information are appropriately detailed and managed via the PHI definitions.
